headline: Sandy Hook starter pack.
subhead: Six key places and routes that define Sandy Hook CT local living. Swipe.

slides.title: Paugussett State Forest
slides.text: Access miles of hiking trails along Lake Zoar, including sections of Al's Trail for year-round outdoor access.

slides.title: Lake Zoar access
slides.text: Eichler's Cove provides boat slips, a public beach area, and kayak launches right on the Housatonic River system.

slides.title: Sandy Hook Center
slides.text: The downtown hub connects local business storefronts along the Pootatuck River with sidewalks and historic architecture.

slides.title: Treadwell Memorial Park
slides.text: Town park featuring athletic fields, tennis courts, a pool complex, and playground areas off Berkshire Road.

slides.title: Interstate 84 corridors
slides.text: Exits 10 and 11 provide direct highway access toward Danbury, Waterbury, and connection points to Route 34.

slides.title: Annual tree lighting
slides.text: Sandy Hook Center hosts a long-standing December tradition with street lanterns and local choir performances.

caption:
Sandy Hook CT sits along the Pootatuck River with direct access to I-84 and Lake Zoar.

If you are looking at homes in eastern Newtown, knowing the layout helps. You have trails at Paugussett State Forest, waterfront spots at Eichler's Cove, and quick highway access at Exit 10 or 11.

December brings the annual village tree lighting right in the center. It is a quiet, steady part of northern Fairfield County with clear geography and strong access points.
